To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the establishment of the interbank money market in China is a significant step toward a market economy and that it is a necessary step toward a more flexible exchange rate regime.
the central bank has successfully established a set of money markets and has shifted its policy approach from direct control of credits to indirect monetary tools.

the establishment of interbank markets in China has enabled the central government to shift from direct credit controls to indirect monetary instruments, but the effectiveness of the indirect tools is constrained by the institutional factors of exchange rate stability, the structure of banks, the corporate governance of banks, the structure of the state sector, the cost consciousness of the state sector and the structure of the financial sector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the institutional constraints that have limited the effectiveness of China’s monetary policy.
the institutional changes in the Chinese monetary system and their impact on monetary policy.

How has the establishment of money market changed the central bank's monetary policy operations? What are the institutional constraints that limit the effectiveness of the indirect monetary tools? How can the effectiveness of these tools be improved?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
China’s money market is not yet fully established and its monetary policy operations have not been fully institutionalized.
the establishment of the money markets in China has enabled the PBOC to shift its policy tools from direct control over credits, to indirect monetary tools.
the establishment of a modern money market and the development of indirect monetary policy tools have been an important step in the reform and development of the Chinese financial system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the establishment of a modern banking system and a money market is a long and complicated process.
China's monetary policy is still a work in progress and the effectiveness of its monetary instruments is limited by the lack of a fully functioning money market and a flexible exchange rate regime.
the Chinese government is trying to establish an effective monetary policy framework in order to achieve the goal of macroeconomic stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the central bank has to be more proactive in the design of monetary policy operations in order to achieve its policy goals.
the central bank has to be more flexible in the use of its policy instruments and to rely more on the market to achieve monetary policy goals.
the central bank needs to be more proactive in establishing the necessary institutional framework for effective policy implementation.
